companies.name: Dronamics
companies.description: Dronamics designs, builds and operates unmanned aerial systems for a wide range of civilian and dual-use applications.
companies.funding_notes: At least $40M pre-Series A (cumulative from VCs and angels, announced Feb 2023) plus €10M EIC Fund equity (2024) and an undisclosed strategic investment from Asia Air Survey (Apr 2026). amount_raised shows the USD part only; the €10M EIC equity comes on top. Also a €2.5M EIC Accelerator grant (2022). EIC STEP equity of up to €30M was proposed in Jun 2025, pending due diligence. No Series A announced yet.

companies.name: Scan.com
companies.description: Find private scanning centres near you, book online from £180 without referral, at the UK's largest private MRI, CT and Ultrasound scan provider. Was National MRI Scan.
companies.funding_notes: Formerly National MRI Scan. About $149M total equity: Forbes puts funding before the Series C at $59M (including a $43M Series B led by YZR, around Dec 2023), plus the $90M Series C led by Noteus (Aug 2026). The Series C came with $130M of debt (VerisFi, Atempo), making $220M in total. The Series B amount and date come only from the Forbes profile; I didn't find a press release for it.

companies.name: Tembo
companies.description: Multi award-winning mortgage & savings platform trusted by thousands of home buyers, voted Best Mortgage Broker five years running by our customers.
companies.funding_notes: About £37.5M total raised: £2.5M seed (2021), £5M Series A (2023), £14M Series B led by Goodwater (Nov 2024; Fieldfisher says this took the total to £20M), and a £16M round led by Gresham House (Feb 2026; no series letter given).

companies.name: Monolith AI
companies.description: Use Monolith AI software to build self-learning models to predict design performance, test less, learn more, and develop better quality products faster.​

grants.name: Innovate UK grant (manufacturability research with Imperial Dyson School of Design Engineering)

companies.funding_notes: About £31.4M total raised: £1.9M seed (2019), £8.5M Series A led by Insight Partners (2021) and £21M Series B (2025; investors not confirmed here). An Imperial College spinout. CoreWeave agreed to acquire it in Oct 2025 for an undisclosed price.

companies.name: Valarian
companies.funding_notes: $70M total raised: $20M total seed (announced May 2025 when it came out of stealth; includes a ~$7M strategic round co-led by Scout and Artis) and a $50M Series A led by NEA (Jul 2026). London-based sovereign AI/defence infrastructure company (ACRA platform).

companies.name: Peptone
companies.description: Peptone is building a Product Engine to generate small-molecule drug candidates against intrinsically disordered proteins.
companies.funding_notes: $40M Series A announced Jun 2022, led by F-Prime and Bessemer. Companies House SH01 filings (via Tero) show three priced allotments totalling £32.2M: seed £1.8M (Nov 2020), Series A-1 £11.4M (Apr 2022) and Series A-2 £19.0M (Sep 2023). The A-2 may be the second tranche of the announced $40M rather than new money. No round announced after 2023; it has an Evotec partnership (2025).

companies.name: Storyblok
companies.description: Storyblok is an intuitive content management system that helps your developer and marketing teams get value from your content faster and create innovative digital experiences.
companies.funding_notes: $138M total raised, per the company at its Series C: $8.5M Series A (2021), $47M Series B (2022) and $80M Series C led by Brighton Park (Jun 2024). Headless CMS based in Linz, Austria. The listed rounds add up to $135.5M; the rest is earlier seed money.

companies.name: Perlego
companies.description: Save up to 90% on textbooks. Read over 1.5 million professional and academic ebooks in one simple space.
companies.funding_notes: $75M total raised, per Tech.eu at the Series C: £7M (~$9M) Series A (2019), $50M Series B led by Mediahuis Ventures (2022) and $20M round led by Sir Terry Leahy (Oct 2024). FinSMEs and Seedtable call that last round a Series C; Tech.eu just calls it the latest round.

companies.name: Circeus
companies.description: Circeus is the AI-native holding company for mission-critical software, bringing frontier AI to the everyday economy through its expanding portfolio.
companies.funding_notes: Holding company of Shop Circle, renamed Circeus in Jun 2026. The company says it has raised more than $120M in equity and more than $220M of total capital, including a $100M+ credit facility from i80 Group. The Shop Circle 'Series A' (Sep 2023) was $120M of mixed equity and debt; its equity share wasn't disclosed. The EBRD-led equity round (Jun 2026) was also undisclosed. amount_raised is the company's 'more than $120M' equity figure. It has made 18 acquisitions.

companies.name: Byway
companies.funding_notes: £5M Series A led by Heartcore (Jul 2024). Before that, a £1.1M package (Jul 2021) combined an Innovate UK SMART grant with Founders Factory and angel money; the grant/equity split wasn't disclosed, so amount_raised counts only the Series A. Including the 2021 package, the total is about £6.1M.

companies.name: Landvault
companies.funding_notes: About $40M total raised: The Block says it had $37M before a $3M Series B extension (Mar 2023), which followed a $25M Series B (Nov 2021). Earlier rounds weren't itemised. Infinite Reality acquired it in a $450M deal (Jul 2024); Infinite Reality later became Napster, which is why the website is now napster.ai.

companies.name: Flourish
companies.description: Bring data to life with Flourish. Create data visualizations and interactive content â no coding needed. Engage, inspire, and tell your best data stories with ease.
companies.funding_notes: £800k (~$1M) seed from LocalGlobe and Founder Collective (Mar 2017). It grew out of the Kiln data-visualisation studio. Canva acquired it in Feb 2022 for an undisclosed price.

companies.name: Calvin Risk
companies.description: Governance risk and compliance platform to enable enterprises to safely deploy AI across their organisation
companies.funding_notes: $4M seed co-led by Join Capital and seed + speed Ventures (Nov 2024). The company says total funding is more than $5M; earlier pre-seed money wasn't itemised. Zurich-based ETH spin-off.

companies.name: Squadded
companies.description: Social shopping solution for eCommerce allowing users to shop and interact with other shoppers.
companies.funding_notes: Social-commerce platform, apparently based in Tel Aviv. Took part in the Founders Factory accelerator (amount undisclosed). Aggregators list an unverified ~$2M round (Feb 2022), but I found no press release or news coverage.

companies.name: Bewica
companies.description: Helping SMEs understand the risk from cybercrime, providing tools and insurance to reduce and manage this risk
companies.funding_notes: Undisclosed angel 'seed' investment from the Angel Academe network (Oct 2020), plus Founders Factory accelerator backing. No priced institutional round found. Other reported amounts (£2M on one site, $180k total on CB Insights) are unverified.

companies.name: Qardus
companies.description: The UK's ethical business lending P2P marketplace
companies.funding_notes: Raised £318,837 in a Seedrs EIS crowdfunding campaign (Jul 2023); the campaign page later shows about £338.7k from 213 investors. It was targeting a £2M+ seed in Dec 2022, but I found no report that it closed. Sharia-compliant P2P business lender.

companies.name: Risparmier
companies.description: AI financial saving agent embedded in your inbox
companies.funding_notes: Risparmier.AI, Milan, founded 2025: an AI savings agent that cuts fixed costs for Italian SMEs. Listed as 'Seed Stage' on F4's startup page, but no amount or round announced. Probably part of the Mediobanca/Founders Factory programme; no disclosed funding found.

companies.name: Connexa
companies.description: Transforming Italian motor insurance with IoT tech and digital innovation.
companies.funding_notes: AutoConnexa (Connexa InsTech), an Italian motor-insurance insurtech. It closed a €4.4M equity raise led by Lumen II with CDP VC and Crédit Agricole (Feb 2026), on top of SAFEs from early 2025, for 'over €6M' in total. The SAFE amount wasn't disclosed. The 2026 round is priced institutional equity, but no stage label (seed or Series A) was published.

companies.name: Previse
companies.description: Artificial Intelligence platform that enables corporates to safely ensure they pay all their suppliers instantly.
companies.funding_notes: About $36M across the announced rounds: $7M Series A (2018), $11M led by Reefknot and Mastercard (Apr 2020) and an $18M first close of a Series B led by Tencent (May 2022). Earlier seed money (Hambro Perks backed it from day one) wasn't itemised. Don't confuse it with Previse, the Baltimore cancer-diagnostics company.

companies.name: Kiro
companies.description: Kiro is your AI money guru and guide, here to answer all your financial questions.

grants.name: Standard Chartered Foundation equity-free grant (VilCap 2026 US Women in Tech Accelerator)

companies.funding_notes: Kiro Money. Raised $200k from Founders Factory and Aviva (2024), an accelerator-sized pre-seed. Also won a $25k equity-free grant (2026). No priced seed found.

companies.name: Moneycado
companies.description: Savings account designed specifically for travel. It makes saving for travel accessible, fun and rewarding.
companies.funding_notes: Only an undisclosed Founders Factory investment (Aug 2018) through its travel accelerator. The co-founder said in Jan 2020 that they couldn't close the next round, so it is likely inactive.

companies.name: Clarity
companies.description: Portable medical device offering personalised, immersive, sensory stimulation therapy for non-invasive, non-pharmacological treatment for neurodegenerative diseases including fatigue for individuals with MS.
companies.funding_notes: Clarity Technologies (San Francisco/Paris) joined the MSWA x Founders Factory MS & Neurological Care Accelerator in June 2026; that programme advertises an AUD 200,000 investment per startup (terms not published). No other publicly sourced priced round found; aggregator sites claim ~$1.7M raised but this is not confirmed by any press. VR gamma-stimulation MS fatigue trial registered (NCT07310862).

companies.name: Jurnee
companies.description: Unique team building experiences virtually and in person - it specialises in both small team events as well as whole company retreats.
companies.funding_notes: Paris-based corporate events/team-building platform. Its own site lists Angular Ventures and Founders Factory as backers. Data aggregators mention a ~$2M pre-seed (Jan 2022), but no press release or reputable news confirms the amount or round type.

companies.name: ScaleXP
companies.description: Business performance platform which pioneers machine learning advances to help tech companies (particularly SaaS) grow faster
companies.funding_notes: £600K seed (May 2021) led by angel Alex Hirsch with Angel Academe, Cambridge Angels, SyndicateRoom and Founders Factory. Caveat: round is labelled seed but investors are mainly angel networks. Aggregators mention a ~£140K grant (2023) and a small 2025 raise, neither verified in primary sources.

companies.name: Txeya
companies.description: Financial community platform for women and LGBTQ+ founders, with built-in credit, banking account, business support and rewards
companies.funding_notes: Company blog (Apr 2022) announced Founders Factory (accelerator) and the Gaingels syndicate as investors; no amount disclosed. Stage label 'Pre-seed' is inferred from the accelerator/syndicate nature. No priced seed round found.

companies.name: Shepper
companies.description: Platform connecting global clients with distributed network of 'Sheppers' who perform on-demand inspections at far lower cost
companies.funding_notes: $5.4M (£4.2M) Series A in Sept 2018 co-led by Aviva Ventures and Norway's Idekapital. Founders posted that a Series B of over £10M (NOK 120M, including new equity plus loan-note conversions, with a New York PE fund joining) closed in Dec 2022, but this appears only in founder social posts, not press, so its amount is excluded from the total. Total raised shown covers the Series A only. Series B (Dec 2022) is only in founders' own social posts, so it is not recorded as a sourced round.

companies.name: Acre
companies.description: End-to-end, cloud-based platform for mortgage brokers, making home-buying frictionless and pain-free
companies.funding_notes: ~£11.5M total: £5M in 2019 led by Aviva and Sesame Bankhall Group (round type not stated), then £6.5M late seed in Apr 2023 led by McPike Global Family Office with Aviva and Founders Factory. Spun out of Founders Factory's Aviva-partnered studio.

companies.name: Rad Swan
companies.description: Socially conscious brand targeting the haircare and protective styling needs of black women with natural hair
companies.funding_notes: RadSwan (founder Freddie Harrel) raised a £1.5M/$2M seed in Nov 2019 from all-female investors incl. BBG Ventures, Female Founders Fund and angel Hannah Bronfman, after Founders Factory's beauty accelerator. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Mo.health
companies.description: The Robinhood of health insurance, offering affordable, transparent, frictionless health cover to SMEs
companies.funding_notes: Mo.health (Mosaic Health Ltd, London) went through Founders Factory's accelerator (early 2022). No press release or reputable news of a funding round found; data aggregators list a ~$210K seed (Apr 2022), probably the accelerator investment, but this is unverified.

companies.name: Bequest
companies.description: Bringing peace of mind, financial security and wealth creation to all modern families, in one holistic and engaging platform
companies.funding_notes: UK life insurance/wills insurtech (FF Bequest Ltd, a Founders Factory build). £1.7M seed in June 2021 led by Kuvi Capital with Clocktower and Form Ventures; earlier backers included Gen Re, Covea and Founders Factory. Wikipedia lists it as defunct (reportedly stopped operating around 2022). Not the same as US-based Bequest Finance (crypto estates).

companies.name: Metal Light
companies.description: Creating sustainable energy from metal via a metal-air generator technology.

grants.name: PGW / Temple University SBDC Energy Innovation Lab incubator seed funding (up to)

companies.funding_notes: Philadelphia-area metal-air (zinc) generator startup. SOSV/HAX portfolio company (accelerator investment ~2022, amount not disclosed). Won a PGW/Temple SBDC incubator spot in Dec 2021 with up to $30K non-dilutive seed support. Aggregators mention ~$70K in grants, unverified. No priced seed round found.

companies.name: Fountain Money
companies.description: Reinventing wealth management by combining new technology with qualified advisors to help you invest towards your goals.
companies.funding_notes: UK digital wealth/advice app (Techswift Ltd). Reported seed round in Nov 2017 (amount not disclosed), led by Day Cooper Day chairman Patrick Day with Charlotte Street Capital and ex-banker angels (via Finextra). Caveat: angel-led, amount undisclosed. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Confide
companies.description: Specialized whistleblowing solution optimised for user trust and regulatory compliance.
companies.funding_notes: Whistleblowing platform founded by Wirecard whistleblower Pav Gill. Founders Factory Fintech Accelerator (with Aviva) investment in 2023; Business Insider (Mar 2024) reported a $500K pre-seed that it was topping up. The founder said in 2026 that an institutional seed round was planned, but none is publicly reported.

companies.name: Qumata
companies.description: Using digital data to help insurers and employers identify and prevent more than 800 medical risks.
companies.funding_notes: Formerly HealthyHealth. $10M Series A (Jun 2021) led by MMC Ventures, extended by $13M to $23M total Series A (Feb 2022). Total of at least $23M; any pre-Series A seed amounts are not counted.

companies.name: Synthesised
companies.description: Privacy-preserved artificial intelligence tool with applications in finance, healthcare and insurance.
companies.funding_notes: Synthesized (synthesized.io), London. $2.8M seed (Mar 2020) co-led by IQ Capital and Mundi Ventures; $20M Series A (Sep 2025) led by redalpine. ~$22.8M total from the two public rounds. Now positioned as AI test data / QA infrastructure.

companies.name: Indie
companies.description: Connecting the travel industry to the best local-led & authentic experiences
companies.funding_notes: Indie Travel (indietravel.co), London software for independent tour guides/operators. Peninsula Road disclosed a 2021 pre-seed investment (amount not disclosed); Founders Factory accelerator alum. Aggregators list a ~$1M seed (Sep 2021) with Leo Capital/Fuel Ventures, but no press or company source confirms it.

companies.name: blaenk
companies.description: Offering physical advertising spaces and a content driven online shop, while executing the checkout and drop-shipping process.
companies.funding_notes: _blaenk GmbH (Cologne retail-as-a-service). Seven-figure (exact amount not disclosed) seed in Nov 2020 from MA Ventures (Migros Aare CVC), M&S x Founders Factory, Ruddat Grund plus existing AC+X and BitStone. Insolvency proceedings opened May 2025 (Cologne court, 70a IN 88/25).

companies.name: Ogma
companies.description: AI-simulated speech and language therapy for children
companies.funding_notes: Founders Factory venture-studio build (AI speech and language therapy for children). No external funding round disclosed. Acquired by Saltroad (UK SLT provider) in June 2026, alongside Saltroad's £1.5M raise led by Techstart Ventures; acquisition terms not disclosed. That £1.5M went to Saltroad, not Ogma.

companies.name: Kinhub
companies.description: Intelligent support system for working parents, providing evidence-based, judgement-free support that empowers all parents to improve their mental health and foster healthy early development in their children.
companies.funding_notes: London employee wellness/parent support platform (founder Erika Brodnock). TechCrunch (Sep 2023) said it was raising a $2.5M seed, with some US investors committed; no close was ever publicly reported. Aggregators list a ~$630K angel round via SyndicateRoom (early 2024) and a ~£170K grant, neither confirmed in primary sources. Founders Factory accelerator alum.

companies.name: Nila
companies.description: Healthcare management platform that helps immigrants care for the elderly parents back home
companies.funding_notes: Nila Cares (London), spun out of Founders Factory's Aviva fintech venture studio. $2.4M (£1.8M) pre-seed (Oct 2025) led by LocalGlobe with Redbus Ventures and angels from Nala, Revolut and Wise. No seed round yet.

companies.name: Inaza
companies.description: Enabling insurers to launch flexible UBI and data-driven motor insurance products quickly, at scale and at a reasonable cost
companies.funding_notes: Dublin insurtech (originally telematics/UBI motor insurance, now an AI data platform for P&C claims and underwriting). CEO Niall Crowley said in Mar 2025 it had raised 'over €1.9M'. Recognised as an Enterprise Ireland High Potential Start-Up. Round breakdown isn't public; aggregators mention a ~€540K angel-backed 'seed' (Dec 2021), unverified.

companies.name: Glimpse
companies.description: The only Net Zero publishing solution for programmatic advertising

grants.name: Innovate UK support (named as a backer alongside the seed round; amount not disclosed)

companies.funding_notes: Glimpse Protocol Ltd (privacy-first/net-zero ad tech). £1.3M seed (Jan 2021) led by Force Over Mass with angels Simon Franks (LoveFilm) and Eric Salama (ex-Kantar), plus Innovate UK support. Caveat: UKTN's £1.3M figure may include the Innovate UK money. No later rounds found. Companies House shows the company dissolved on 21 Jan 2025.
